interest: This file offers an illuminating glimpse into the emerging 'reverse course' in U.S. occupation policy toward Japan during mid-1947, showcasing the acute bureaucratic tensions between the War Department and the State Department over reparations and economic recovery. Assistant Secretary of War Howard C. Petersen's correspondence reveals the War Department's willingness to contemplate unilateral U.S. action and bypass the eleven-nation Far Eastern Commission by engaging private American engineering firms (Overseas Consultants, Inc., headed by Clifford S. Strike) to re-evaluate and challenge earlier punitive industrial removal targets (such as SWNCC 236/43). In contrast, the concurrent adoption of FEC-084/19 and the accompanying Chinese reservation highlight the diplomatic friction between Asian allies demanding substantial industrial reparations for wartime devastation and American military planners increasingly intent on reviving Japan's industrial economy.
overview: This file (July 22 – August 21, 1947) covers high-level U.S. interdepartmental negotiations and multilateral Far Eastern Commission (FEC) actions concerning Japanese reparations, level-of-industry standards, and the reduction of Japan's industrial war potential. The early portion contains an exchange between Assistant Secretary of War Howard C. Petersen and Assistant Secretary of State John H. Hilldring resolving differences over the War Department's contract with Overseas Consultants, Inc. (headed by Clifford S. Strike) to perform an independent engineering survey and audit of Japanese industrial plants without contravening approved U.S. policies like SWNCC 236/43 or Allied commitments. The latter portion consists of Far Eastern Commission Policy Decision FEC-084/19 (unanimously adopted August 14, 1947) defining rules for the destruction, reparations removal, and permissible retention levels of Japanese primary and war-supporting industries, accompanied by an interpretive statement by China and a State Department transmittal memorandum routing the resulting draft directive through SWNCC and the Joint Chiefs of Staff to General Douglas MacArthur (SCAP).

subfiles.about: Clarifies the War Department's rationale for hiring Overseas Consultants, Inc. to audit plant selections for Japanese reparations and addresses State Department concerns regarding unilateral action.
subfiles.from: Howard C. Petersen, Assistant Secretary of War
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary of War Petersen responds to Assistant Secretary of State Hilldring's memorandum of July 15, expressing surprise that earlier understandings regarding the Overseas Consultants, Inc. contract are being questioned. He explains that an independent engineering audit, headed by Clifford S. Strike, was requested by General MacArthur to certify plant selections for reparations and assess Japan's required level of industry. Petersen argues that unilateral U.S. action may become necessary if the Far Eastern Commission fails to act promptly, and notes that the data will be valuable for the upcoming peace conference. He warns that public speculation over pending leadership retirements has caused concern among the participating engineering firms and requests an urgent conference to maintain the contract.
subfiles.title: Letter from Howard C. Petersen to John H. Hilldring on Overseas Consultants Contract and Industrial Survey
subfiles.to: John H. Hilldring, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Announces the War Department's engagement of Overseas Consultants, Inc. to evaluate Japan's industrial potential and assets available for reparations removals.
subfiles.summary: The War Department announces that Assistant Secretary of War Howard C. Petersen has engaged Overseas Consultants, Incorporated, a consortium of eleven major American engineering and appraisal firms, to survey Japanese industrial potential and reparations availability. The release notes that the consortium is led by Clifford S. Strike, former Deputy for Reparations in Germany, following a request by General MacArthur for an independent audit. Petersen indicates that the contract allows MacArthur to leverage leading American industrial experts to help resolve complex Far Eastern economic issues.
subfiles.title: War Department Press Release on Overseas Consultants Survey of Japanese Industry

subfiles.about: Expresses satisfaction that differences between the State and War Departments regarding the Overseas Consultants mission have been resolved.
subfiles.from: John H. Hilldring, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Hilldring replies to Petersen's letter of July 24, welcoming the resolution of misunderstandings concerning the Strike Corporation Mission to Japan. He notes that the proposed modifications to the instructions for Overseas Consultants, Inc. fully satisfy the State Department. Hilldring also requests that the corporation's interim reports be transmitted regularly to the State Department on the same basis as SCAP to assist in formulating U.S. policy in the Far Eastern Commission and guiding decisions on reparations.
subfiles.title: Letter from John H. Hilldring to Howard C. Petersen Resolving Differences over Strike Mission
subfiles.to: Howard C. Petersen, Assistant Secretary of War

subfiles.about: Sets forth specific instructions to be issued to Overseas Consultants, Inc. regarding adherence to SWNCC 236/43 and approved policy decisions.
subfiles.from: Howard C. Petersen, Assistant Secretary of War
subfiles.summary: Petersen outlines the specific instructions that the Secretary of War will issue to Overseas Consultants, Inc. under Article 1 e of their contract to avoid the delays of formal contract amendment. The instructions clarify that Overseas Consultants, Inc. is not hired to determine or challenge the level of industry set in SWNCC 236/43, but should record in their report any specific errors they identify. The firm will be directed to follow SWNCC 236/43 and relevant U.S. and FEC policy decisions. Petersen notes that once Hilldring confirms agreement, copies of the instructions will be officially sent to the corporation's president and to General MacArthur.
subfiles.title: Letter from Howard C. Petersen to John H. Hilldring Defining Operational Instructions for Overseas Consultants
subfiles.to: John H. Hilldring, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Transmits the Far Eastern Commission's unanimously adopted policy decision on Japanese industrial war potential reduction and a Chinese statement for implementation by SCAP.
subfiles.from: Samuel S. Stratton, Acting Secretary General, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.summary: Stratton officially transmits to Acting Secretary of State Lovett the certified text of the policy decision on the reduction of Japanese industrial war potential adopted unanimously at the FEC's 70th meeting on August 14, 1947. He requests that the U.S. Government prepare the appropriate directives and transmit them to General MacArthur in accordance with the Commission's Terms of Reference. Stratton also encloses an interpretive statement entered into the minutes by the Chinese representative, requesting that it accompany the directive to Tokyo, and notes the Commission's plan to release the policy decision to the press once received by SCAP.
subfiles.title: Letter from Samuel S. Stratton to Robert A. Lovett Transmitting FEC Policy Decision on Reduction of Japanese Industrial War Potential
subfiles.to: Robert A. Lovett, Acting Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Establishes Allied policy governing the destruction, reparations removal, and capacity limitations of Japan's war and war-supporting industries.
subfiles.summary: This comprehensive policy decision sets forth detailed measures to eliminate Japan's war-making potential during the occupation. It mandates the destruction of all specialized combat-equipment machinery and provides that primary war facilities, as well as excess capacity in designated war-supporting industries (including steel, chemicals, shipbuilding, and machine tools), be made available for reparations. Permissible productive capacity ceilings are established until October 1, 1949, or the conclusion of the current occupation phase, subject to subsequent FEC review and peace treaty terms. The Supreme Commander is authorized to grant temporary retention exceptions for occupation necessities after consulting the Allied Council for Japan and is instructed to maintain complete records of all removals and destruction.
subfiles.title: Far Eastern Commission Policy Decision FEC-084/19: Reduction of Japanese Industrial War Potential
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (via U.S. Government)

subfiles.about: Records the official statement of the Chinese representative regarding the interpretation and implementation of FEC-084/19.
subfiles.from: Chinese Delegation to the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.summary: An excerpt from the draft minutes of the 70th FEC meeting records the Chinese Government's understanding of key clauses in the policy decision on industrial war potential reduction. China notes that the phrase 'present phase of occupation' corresponds strictly to the existing control regime established by the FEC and Allied Council for Japan. It further stipulates that any delays in reparations removals or disarmament decisions before October 1, 1949, must not diminish the total reparations pool or adversely affect the allocation shares of claimant nations. The statement also clarifies that paragraph 5 b (2) encompasses machinery used to manufacture heavy prime movers, cranes, mining equipment, and chemical apparatus.
subfiles.title: Excerpt from FEC Draft Minutes: Chinese Statement on Reduction of Japanese Industrial War Potential

subfiles.about: Transmits the draft directive based on FEC-084/19 to SWNCC for forwarding through the Joint Chiefs of Staff to General MacArthur.
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, Special Assistant to the Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Saltzman transmits to the Secretary of SWNCC the draft directive formulated from the Far Eastern Commission's August 14 policy decision on reducing Japanese industrial war potential. He requests that SWNCC forward the directive to the Joint Chiefs of Staff for transmission to General MacArthur, noting that any JCS queries should be referred back to the State Department. He also requests that SCAP be provided with the Chinese representative's statement of understanding and informed of the requirement to acknowledge receipt so the policy decision can be released to the press.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Charles E. Saltzman to SWNCC Transmitting Draft Directive on Reduction of Japanese Industrial War Potential
